data.title: Vibe Coding
data.tagline: Building software by describing the desired result to an AI agent and reviewing the work it makes
data.learningOutcome: You can describe a scoped change, ask for evidence, and verify the result instead of treating generated code as automatically correct.
data.description: You can ask an agent to build a settings page, inspect the changed files, then test the mobile layout. It can speed up implementation, but you still need to define the scope, check the result, and protect data and secrets.

learning.assumes: You have asked an AI assistant to change a page or write code.
learning.outcome: You can describe a scoped change, ask for evidence, and verify the result instead of treating generated code as automatically correct.

explanation.title: Describe the observable result
explanation.text: State what should change, what must stay untouched, and where the problem appears.

explanation.title: Give the agent usable context
explanation.text: Provide the relevant files, constraints, and test result instead of asking it to guess.

explanation.title: Verify the delivered work
explanation.text: Review the changed files and test the requested behavior at the needed screen sizes.

data.boundary: Vibe coding is a way of collaborating with an AI agent, not a substitute for product decisions, security checks, or real testing.

lessonPractice.title: An AI-built event signup page works locally, and the team plans to collect real names and phone numbers tomorrow. What is the better next step?

options.label: Pause feature work, inspect data flow, permissions, and dependencies, add critical tests, and have a person review the changes
options.feedback: Correct. A working local screen proves only that the prototype runs. Software handling real personal data needs formal review and verification.

options.label: Keep accepting every AI change and ship as soon as the page shows no error
options.feedback: No visible error does not establish safe data handling, authorization, or failure behavior.

options.label: Polish colors and animation first, then treat visual completion as proof that the feature is reliable
options.feedback: Visual polish says nothing about correct storage or access control and cannot replace technical checks.

data.agentPrompt: I want to vibe-code a weekend prototype using fake data only, with no accounts, payments, or real user information. Build the smallest runnable version first, then run the project and check the actual result after every change. Stop and tell me before using real data, secrets, or irreversible actions. When it works, list what still needs review and testing before release.
